scope.summary: Extend the Glue/Tack placement handler to validate and store multi-point tack arrays, enforce per-tack r_local derivation from tack_anchor_json defaults when tack positions are unspecified, and expose the multi-anchor authoring path in the operator UI and MCP tool input schema
acceptance_criteria: When tack anchor positions are omitted, the handler reads tack_anchor_json from tailor_trims and uses those body-local offsets as the default r_local for each GpuTackConstraint per TR-6.1.5
Multi-point tack placements (e.g., 4-hole button with 4 tacks) generate exactly N GpuTackConstraint entries where N = length of tacks_json array
TACK_SEAM_CLOSURE validation check (TR-11.1) correctly evaluates all N tack distances at end of draping
TailorTrimTackUpdated event is emitted when an existing placement's tacks_json is modified
The place_trim MCP tool (MT-263) input schema accepts an optional tack_anchors field as a list of panel-local UV positions

All operator-facing scope is implemented in src/frontend/handshake_native with native wgpu/egui, AccessKit author_id, Argus inspection/steering/capture, and no Tailor React, Tauri-command, WebView, data-testid-only, or rendered-PNG frontend path.

The exact TailorSurfaceDescriptor row MT-365 enumerates every route, pane, control author_id, dynamic entity-key rule, action, state, help anchor, permission, undo policy, receipt, and command binding; wildcard-only evidence is rejected.

Applicable blank, loading, populated, stale/conflict, cancelled, failed, retry, permission, keyboard/focus, narrow/4K/DPI, overlap/clipping, and no-focus-steal states are covered by the registry-derived Argus matrix.
scope.risk_if_missed: Four-hole buttons, rivets, and any trim with multiple attachment points will silently use a single default tack, producing physically incorrect simulation (trim rotates freely instead of being pinned at all holes); TACK_SEAM_CLOSURE check cannot be meaningful with only one constraint per multi-anchor trim

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

surfaces: native Tailor pane and applicable editor, viewport, browser, timeline, or status surface

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > Trims, closures, and rigid attachments

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

required_changes_before_execution: Replace contradictory CPU/GPU trim ownership with the per-tier interaction matrix and require final two-way generalized-coordinate coupling where the selected profile needs it.
Replace legacy app/src or app/src-tauri targets with the native Handshake shell and native Tailor paths.
Added gui_obligation, user_manual_obligation, and HBR-INT-009 tier obligations from the current MT template without removing original scope.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.

Use authenticated SurrealDB record-user table/field PERMISSIONS intersected with ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; administrative/root credentials and UI filtering are never the security boundary. PostgreSQL and SQLite access paths are forbidden.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
